title: OpenAI Responses schema fidelity, streaming behavior hypotheses, and migration playbook
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Investigate and mitigate behavioral deltas between Redwood's Responses-compatible runtime and the OpenAI Responses API when handling streaming events, tool/function calling signals, and structured output schemas. Deliver an instrumentation-first migration playbook with a lightweight runtime shim, observable hypothesis testing, and a minimal-risk rollout path for customers migrating from OpenAI Responses semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry that identifies the top 5 classes of event-level mismatch with >95% confidence for representative workloads
A prototype 'event-normalizer' shim that rewrites OpenAI-style response streams to Redwood canonical events with <2ms median added latency
Migration guide and SDK flag (responses.compat="true") that preserves tool-call fidelity for 3 representative customer integrations
End-to-end automated test harness that validates streaming boundaries, tool-call invocation/return semantics, and structured JSON schema preservation against a suite of 50 prompts
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, SDK, and Observability. Agreed on hypothesis-driven approach: enumerate deltas, instrument, test, iterate.

2026-02-18: Added protobuf of proposed telemetry events (resp.request_start, resp.stream_chunk, resp.tool_call_start, resp.tool_call_end, resp.schema_violation). Initial Datadog metrics dashboard sketched.
2026-02-25: Implemented lightweight instrumentation in runtime: emitted stream_chunk events for streaming tokens and final_event markers. Telemetry sent to kinesis-testing for analysis.

2026-03-02: Observed hypothesis H1: OpenAI stream sometimes emits tool_call metadata in a separate final event; our runtime currently emits tool_call only when the token stream includes a canonical 'tool' marker -> causes missing invocation logs in 12% of traces.
2026-03-05: Prototype event-normalizer v0.1 implemented (runtime gateway rewrite). Microbenchmarked: added median +1.8ms latency with p95 +4.2ms. Created PR #7124.
2026-03-09: Design review with PM and Security. Agreed to gate full rollout behind schema_violation metric thresholds and opt-in SDK flag.
2026-03-12: Canary plan approved: 5% of test-customer traffic routed through shim with enhanced tracing and synthetic prompts to validate behavior. Instrumentation dashboards ready.
comments: PM (Jordan Lee): Emphasize low-friction migration for customers using tool-calling libraries. Need clear opt-out and rollback instructions.
Design (Marta Alvarez): For structured output differences, propose a 'TypedJSON' adapter that validates and, where safe, coerces types. UX must clearly surface coercions in the Console.
Security (Nina Gupta): Gateway rewrite must not log PII. Ensure schema_violation events are redacted and sampled. KMS gating for any persisted payloads.
Infra (Samir Okoye): Watch out for increased KV-cache churn if shim introduces synthetic prefixes. Add cache-hit metrics to the dashboard.
Reviewer (Ravi Patel): Need unit tests for edge cases: nested tool-calls, streamed JSON chunks that split tokens inside structural characters, and ambiguous function name collisions.
notes: We intentionally avoid deep protocol translation that changes semantics; the shim is a minimal event-normalizer to preserve customer-visible behavior.
Plan includes a fallback gateway that can switch between 'strict' (Redwood canonical) and 'compat' (OpenAI-like) modes per-tenant.
SDK flag proposal: SDK.responses_compat = 'openai-v1' | 'redwood-canonical' | 'auto' (default 'auto' during canary).
Consider adding a small cost pass-through when shim is enabled (covering telemetry/transform costs).
risk_mitigation: Canary only 5% traffic with automated rollback on >0.5% schema_violation increase or >2x error-rate delta.
Do not persist full request bodies for schema_violation events—only hashes and redacted snippets sampled at 0.1%.
Expose immediate toggle in Console for affected customers; Customer Success notified ahead of canary start.
test_plan: Unit tests for event-normalizer token reassembly (including cases where JSON structures are split across chunks)
Integration tests that simulate tool-calling chains with nested calls and validate call/return pairing
Load tests at scale to ensure shim adds acceptable overhead at p99 latency budgets
Golden-file tests: compare Redwood canonical output vs shimmed OpenAI-style stream on a corpus of 250 prompts
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Run synthetic canary on staging with 1000 synthetic users. Duration 72h.
Phase 1 (limited beta): 5% production traffic for invited customers for 7 days. Monitor schema_violation, errors, latency.
Phase 2 (expanded beta): 25% production traffic for additional customers, enable SDK.compat opt-in in Console.
Phase 3 (GA): Default to auto mode with opt-out; announce migration guide and deprecation window for older SDK versions.
